Resolute

/RES-uh-loot/ — rhymes with absolute · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is resolute is firmly determined and unwilling to give up, even when facing doubt or difficulty.

Despite three rejections, the resolute inventor kept refining her design.

Worked Example

The climber pushed through exhaustion and mounting doubt on the mountain, refusing to turn back despite the gathering storm.

Resolute is more precise than 'determined' because it emphasizes not just the intention to reach a goal, but the unwillingness to abandon it despite facing obstacles and internal doubt. Resolute captures that firmness in the face of adversity.

How Resolute Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

determined

determined: firmly set on reaching a chosen goal

steadfast

steadfast: loyally firm and unchanging over time

unyielding

unyielding: refusing to bend under pressure or opposition

Antonyms

wavering

wavering: uncertainly shifting back and forth between choices

hesitant

hesitant: holding back, unsure whether to act

How Strong Is It? — willing → determined → resolute → unflinching

willing vs. resolute

willing vs. resolute: Willing is much weaker than resolute: a willing person simply agrees to try, while a resolute person is firmly committed to seeing the goal through.

determined vs. resolute

determined vs. resolute: Determined is strong, but resolute is stronger — a determined person works hard toward a goal, while a resolute person cannot be shaken from it even by repeated failure.

unflinching vs. resolute

unflinching vs. resolute: Unflinching is even stronger than resolute: a resolute person holds firm to a decision, while an unflinching one shows no trace of hesitation even in the face of danger.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back, again (used here to intensify) (Latin)

Root — solut

Root — solut: loosened, untied (from solvere, 'to loosen') (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Resolute comes from Latin resolvere, 'to loosen or break apart completely.' Untangling a question down to its parts lets you settle it once and for all — so resolute came to mean firmly decided and determined, unwilling to give up.

Use the root in a new word: solution

Use the root in a new word: solution: When you find the solution to a puzzle, you 'loosen' its knot — the same Latin root solvere hides inside resolute, someone whose mind is firmly settled after working the problem through.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Resolute is more formal and elevated than the everyday word 'determined.' Use it when you want to emphasize that someone has firmly made up their mind and won't waver despite real obstacles and self-doubt. For simple determination without those added layers, 'determined' is the plainer choice.
